guitar.modelsText: Gibson Flying V / Harmony Meteor / Telecaster
guitar.notes: Dave Davies famously slashed his amp speaker for distortion using a Harmony/Telecaster-type setup; reasonably documented, medium confidence is fair.

tone.target: jangly dry British Invasion rhythm with light Vox chime
tone.profile: jangly dry British Invasion rhythm with light Vox chime
tone.summary: A classic British Invasion rhythm tone achieved with light overdrive (Green OD), followed by the UK 45 amp model, paired with the UK Vintage 4x12 cabinet for that signature Vox-like chime and dry punch.

rig.name: The Kinks - Sunny Afternoon - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide light, natural breakup and twangy attack without heavy distortion.
Emulate the bright, punchy sound of a Vox AC30/British rhythm amp.
Provide the classic British cabinet sound and bright upper-mid bite.
Enhance the upper-mids and brightness while keeping the tone dry.
Avoid chorus as per the musical verdict.
Avoid deep delay to maintain a dry mono feel.
Add a small amount of natural space without sounding wet or modern.
blocks.gap: The verdict asks for 'dry mono feel', so reverb is kept minimal and subtle.

improvements.summary: Swap IR for a more open-back, single-coil focused cabinet to enhance the Vox chime and dry punch.

proposals.recommendedAsset: open-back 2x12 or UK AC30 style IR
proposals.reason: Enhance open-back, single-coil focused Vox chime and dry punch.
